history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: 'Hubli' is the anglicized name of Hubballi; the temple stands at Rayapur on the Hubballi-Dharwad road, Dharwad district. On Sri Ramanavami 2002 the panchaloha utsava deities of Sri Krishna Balarama, Sri Gaura Nitai and Srila Prabhupada (carved in Vrindavan) were installed in a rented building at Lingarajnagar, Hubli. The Government of Karnataka allotted ~8.2-8.5 acres at Rayapur (2005), and the deities were moved to a makeshift temple there in 2006; Sri Lakshmi Narasimha deities were installed in May 2015. Bhoomi puja (2011) and shilanyasa (2013) were performed for a new Sri Radha Krishna Temple and Cultural Complex on the site; a YouTube vlog claims the new complex was inaugurated 22 June 2026 - UNVERIFIED by official sources (verify). The centre runs an Akshaya Patra kitchen, goshala and cultural programmes.

name: ISKCON Sri Krishna Balarama Temple
town_description: Hubballi (formerly Hubli), twinned with Dharwad as the Hubballi-Dharwad municipal corporation, is the commercial and educational hub of North Karnataka. It is a major rail and road junction on NH-48 between Bengaluru and Pune, known for its BRTS bus corridor, the large Akshaya Patra centralised kitchen, and a strong base of educational and cultural institutions.

travel.road: On the Hubballi-Dharwad (PB) Road at Rayapur, beside the Bengaluru-Pune NH-48 bypass; served by the Hubballi-Dharwad BRTS bus route (verify).
